1.2.1.1-f11.accuracy_reason: Persius 3.65 reads 'et quid opus Cratero magnos promittere montis?'; Craterus was a well-known physician, also named by Horace and Cicero.

1.2.1.1-f12.accuracy_reason: Ovid, Remedia amoris 44, reads 'una manus vobis vulnus opemque feret'. The spear of Achilles, which healed the wound it made in Telephus, is correctly explained.

1.2.1.1-f7.accuracy_reason: 'ad classica' is right (De III cons. Honorii 98). But the lines speak to Honorius ('cui… cui'), praising him as heaven's favourite, so the note's 'fighting on Theodosius's side' is only loosely right (the battle, at the Frigidus, was Theodosius's).

1.2.1.1-f8.accuracy_reason: Theodoret (HE 3.20/25) does report Julian's 'Vicisti, Galilaee', and the words are rightly called legendary.
